source_snapshot.criteria: Policy matches; SUT powers on after AC return; post-CPU-swap SUT powers on successfully.
source_snapshot.script: Private power-policy-always-power-on; 10 attended and 20 machine minutes; source requests log clearing.

historical_reviews.deepseek: The command fragment sets the intended policy but the narrative oracle is wrong, secrets are exposed and no reset persistence, physical power behavior, CPU compatibility or recovery is proven.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly requires both pre-loss-state trials to end powered on and isolates the ESD-controlled CPU replacement phase.
historical_reviews.history: No earlier exact source identity record exists.
historical_reviews.v3_1: AlwaysOn is distinguished most clearly by the powered-off pre-loss trial: AC return must cause a new host power-on without operator pressing power. The already-on trial additionally checks a clean recovery rather than a stuck-off or reboot-loop result; neither can be replaced by a policy string.

original_test_intent: Prove AlwaysOn policy persistence across BMC reset and AC loss from both host states, then separately verify controlled post-replacement boot for the approved CPU swap.
original_method: Preserve the initial policy/hardware/workload state, set AlwaysOn through a supported protected interface, verify before and after BMC cold reset, execute separately approved manual AC loss/return trials from on and off with both ending in a healthy powered-on host, then perform the approved ESD-safe CPU service and validate deliberate POST/boot before restoring baseline.
manual_activity: An operator approves and performs BMC/AC operations, observes autonomous power-on after AC return, then separately performs powered-down CPU service and owns recovery and verdict.
required_inputs: Expected boot and readiness timeouts from each pre-loss state
Maintenance window, backup and independent recovery
Exact old/new CPU part and serial matrix
BIOS, microcode, power and thermal compatibility
ESD-safe service and socket recovery procedure
safety_requirements: Use separate approvals for policy, reset, AC and CPU phases
Verify exact PDU outlet and service target
Use protected secrets and supported commands
Keep CPU service fully de-energized and ESD controlled
Stop on unexpected off state, uncontrolled reboot, alarm or POST failure
Never auto-retry power or hardware operations
agent_execution_scope: Verify target and supported AlwaysOn mapping
Monitor reset persistence and autonomous AC-return boot timelines
Collect POST, topology, boot and thermal evidence
engineer_actions: Confirm outlet, backup and autonomous-start expectations
Recover abnormal power or boot state

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The policy command is relevant only under supported mapping and protected authentication; its Last-State wording is wrong and set/readback alone omits every physical and CPU checkpoint.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use protected AlwaysOn set/readback, then independently timestamp operator-controlled AC loss/return from on and off states and verify autonomous host start before the separately gated CPU phase.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The 10/20-minute estimates and all source phases remain; automated physical action and blanket log clearing remain prohibited.

modernized_recommendation.status: PHASED ALWAYSON AUTOSTART AND CPU-SERVICE VALIDATION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build one persistence ledger, two autonomous-start timelines and one CPU-service boot ledger, each with its own approval, abort boundary and recovery proof.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact target/outlet binding, protects credentials, proves autonomous rather than manual start and governs CPU compatibility/restoration.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Set/readback does not demonstrate that power restoration actually asserts host power or that the replacement CPU can boot safely.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: AlwaysOn can unexpectedly start hardware when AC is applied; the service area must be clear and the operator must not mistake manual intervention for policy behavior.

project_override_considerations: The Project must define autonomous-start timing, the compatible CPU pair and issue 1029175 acceptance. CPU replacement remains a separate checkpoint and cannot substitute for either AC scenario.
expected_evidence: Approved target/outlet, baseline policy/hardware, backup and recovery
Protected AlwaysOn set/readback before and after BMC reset
On-pre-loss AC timeline ending in healthy powered-on state
Off-pre-loss timeline proving autonomous power-on without manual host command
CPU identity/ESD service and deliberate POST/boot/topology/health proof
Original policy/CPU/workload restoration, preserved logs and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Master Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently specify AlwaysOn plus a CPU-swap boot checkpoint. DeepSeek's Last-State text is an incorrect review description, not a Master conflict.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Supported policy mapping, controlled PDU access, compatible CPU matrix, backup, ESD service and recovery are requestable prerequisites; execution blocks only if they cannot be provided safely.

review_improvement: Corrects the Last-State oracle and explicitly proves autonomous start while isolating the unrelated physical CPU compatibility phase.
independent_technical_reasoning: The powered-off pre-loss scenario is the decisive AlwaysOn discriminator because no pre-existing running state can explain the post-AC start. Evidence must show the policy, AC edge and host power assertion with no manual command. The powered-on trial checks recovery health, while CPU replacement introduces a separate compatibility state machine and risk boundary.
